precepts.text: When Judas fell and Simon rose up in his stead, the people vowed the same obedience to the new leader, just as Israel did with Joshua after Moses.
precepts.point: The boundary stands: if an order breaks the commandments of God, no. But if it falls within the boundaries of the commandments, be willing without hesitation to do what your leader tells you. Whatever position you hold in the body, you are a servant, and when the opportunity comes to fulfill an order you need to be ready; that readiness is the spirit we lack in Israel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee”. When Judas fell and Simon rose up in his stead, the people vowed the same obedience to the new leader: “Thou shalt be our leader instead of Judas and Jonathan thy brother. Fight thou our battles, and whatsoever, thou commandest us, that will we do.”

Just as Israel did with Joshua after Moses. When a leader falls and a new leader rises in his stead, that is who the Lord appointed over you, and he is owed the same respect the original leader had. Moses himself asked the Lord to select the man; the selection is spiritual.

“Whosoever he be that doth rebel against thy commandment, and will not hearken unto thy words in all that thou commandest him, he shall be put to death”: that is how our forefathers rolled. Under Christ there is grace and mercy, but the order still works by delegation; instruction passes from Christ through the brothers he sets over you, and refusing the brother who carries the order is refusing the one who sent it. Rehearse these righteous acts of taking orders while you have grace.
